terra.problem: The line says God promises to gather worshipers, but Zephaniah 3:10 says His worshipers will bring Him an offering; it does not say He will gather them. The line is also long and abstract for a fifth-grade reader.
“Tirhakah of Cush Marches” concerns the king of Cush, but the passage does not place his march in Cush. Hezekiah spreads the letter before the LORD in Jerusalem, not Cush.
“Cush Reaches Out to God” is a psalm’s future statement about Cush, not an event located in Cush. “Envoys” may also be difficult for fifth-grade readers; “messengers” would be simpler.
“A Sign Against Egypt and Cush” is a sign and warning concerning Cush, but the passage does not say Isaiah performs the sign in Cush or locate the predicted exile there.
“Worshipers from Beyond Cush” describes worshipers coming from beyond the rivers of Cush, not an event happening in Cush. The passage also does not locate the offering in Cush.
